newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares to swing to U.S. beat.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares to swing to U.S. beat.

text.p: Belgian equities will swing to the rhythm of U.S. financial markets for the foreseeable future, dealers said on Friday.

"We will not see any change in monetary policy in Europe in the near future so it depends on what happens in the U.S. on the run up to the November 13 FOMC meeting," one said, referring to the post-U.S. presidential election meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy committee.
An early rise in U.S. stocks on Friday helped Belgian shares to a higher close. "New York has been down in recent days but today it gave support," he said.
However, other analysts were more bullish.
"Now that it has risen above 2,350 francs it is a clear buy," Gert de Mesure at Antwerp brokerage Delen & Co said, referring to the price guaranteed by the put warrant.
"We upgrade our recommendation from 'hold' to 'buy'," Generale Bank said in a statement, noting CBR was fundamentally not expensive.
Outside the Bel-20, hamburger chain Quick ended up 10 francs at 2,200, partially reversing its slide on Thursday on fears over a new French fast food tax.
The Bel-20 leading share index closed up 8.22 points, or 0.47 percent, at 1,773.35 points, just off its session high of 1,773.75 and well above its day low of 1,761.08.
Bel-20 volume of 2.3 billion Belgian francs was dominated for the third day by trade in cement group CBR, where turnover was 251,172 shares.
Total forward market volume was 2.8 billion francs.

CBR, boosted by speculation surrounding the approaching expiry of a put warrant on its share, ended 10 francs higher at 2,390 francs after earlier touching 2,420 francs. One dealer predicted the activity could calm down.
